title: the adapter verdict: a vendor that fails silently is not one that worked
acceptance: an adapter reports unavailable when its CLI prints an outage and exits 0
a finished run whose own output discusses logins, rate limits or 429 is done, not an outage
a verdict reads only the bytes its own run added to the shared fallback log
each adapter is asserted to produce the invocation its CLI documents, not merely to be handed the prompt
the reviewer falls back through the same chain as the worker, from one implementation
no vendor runs twice however the fallback list is written
a review round must carry APPROVE or REJECT; anything else is an engine that failed, exits 3 and emits review_failed
a failed round keeps the engine's log under state/reviews and says where it is
fm-run reports a reviewer that was unavailable or produced no verdict instead of swallowing it
review_failed and worker_crashed read as blocked on the board, in counts as well as lanes
every stage the board maps is a type fm-emit will write
no stage of bin/ci.sh reads standard input, and a suite is handed /dev/null
the hygiene lint is asserted to be linting the suites it was given
no script dispatches a child without closing standard input, proved by a probe that blocks forever if it is open
the gate lints bin/adapters as well as bin, which bin/*.sh does not reach
work in the worktree is never discarded because the verdict read an outage
wording never decides finally: the caller supplies the evidence and work beats a signature
a vendor named in config.yaml with no adapter behind it is a configuration error, not an outage
a fixture that swaps a script out is paired with its restore by the harness, and a hand-rolled one fails the gate
the gate names every script that dispatches without closing standard input
an exit code never overrules produced work, in the adapters or in either caller
every signature is shaped like a failure and is read against a healthy transcript as well as a failing one
a configuration error is found before any vendor runs
each attempt reads only its own output: its own directory and its own slice of the shared log
a file that is meant to be sourced never carries the standard-input redirect
